reader_question: How has the typical household’s income changed, and how sure is each year’s figure?
title: Median household income stood at $87,460 in 2025, in 2025 dollars, the highest since the survey’s first year, 1967.
measure_line: Median household income in 2025 dollars, each year from 1967 to 2025, United States, the whole series. The band spans each year’s 90 percent margin of error.
reading_guide: The line breaks in 2013, where new income questions put the year’s two estimates $2,200 apart. A new processing system in 2017 put them $300 apart, too close to show as a break; the table prints both.
notes: The 2025 figure carries a margin of error of plus or minus $1,040 at 90 percent confidence; its rise over 2024’s $85,210 passes the margin of the gap.
Income before taxes, from the Current Population Survey’s Annual Social and Economic Supplement, adjusted for inflation to 2025 dollars.
alt: A line of median household income from 1967 to 2025 in 2025 dollars, with a light band for each year’s margin of error. It rises from $56,230 in 1967 to $87,460 in 2025, the highest of the series, and breaks in 2013, where new survey questions put the year’s two estimates $2,200 apart. In 2017 a new processing system put them $300 apart, too close to show as a break.
chart_notes: The light band around the line spans each year’s margin of error. In 2013 and 2017 the line breaks and draws both of the year’s estimates as dots; 2025 is labeled at the line’s end.
